items.title: Difference Between Propositional and Predicate Logic

source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Difference Between Propositional and Predicate Logic under 2.8, as printed (PDF 31, printed 27).

blocks.text: Propositional logic deals with simple statements that are either true or false. It cannot describe properties of objects or relationships between them. Predicate logic, on the other hand, uses predicates and variables to express detailed statements. Predicate logic is more expressive and powerful than propositional logic. Propositional logic is easier to understand but less flexible. Predicate logic allows statements about many objects and conditions.
